rule_questions.question: Does a not-yet-tried 'looks so nice' (an impression from photos) count as a stated positive or as opinion none?
Same as the S&P case: an untried 'looks so good, gonna order' reply; should it be none or an endorse?

A comment attacking the chef (David Chang) personally, under a Momofuku thread, without naming or judging the restaurant: I treated it as no mention; should a knock on the owner count against the place?
When a bare list answers 'easiest places to walk in', should the post's framing set wait positive on each endorsement, or do endorsements keep all aspects null?
When the only remark is a wait complaint put as a fact ('line started at 4:15'), should overall stay null or follow the strongest point to negative?
Untried-place impressions ('looks tasty', 'looks so good') recur often; the rubric should say whether they are stated levels or opinion none.
Zabar's (a grocery store with a famous deli counter) praised for its deli pickles: grocery store excluded, or a deli mention?
A chain used as a rhetorical jab in an argument (McDonald's 'pink slime' nuggets): should it count as a judged mention, and is 'pink slime' extreme enough for very_negative?
Supermarkets praised for prepared food (Pomegranate's chicken salad, Zabar's pickles): exclude as grocery stores even when the comment gives no hint that they are stores?
'That is what I was afraid of' under a 'too spicy' complaint about an untried place: an agreement reply (stated, negative) or a worry/question (none)?
When the place is named only in an ancestor Haiku did not see, should the missed object still be listed (as here), given Haiku could not have named it?
Is a packaged-food brand (Grillo's Pickles) that runs a one-off NYC pop-up a mention, or a product like a grocery item?
When the commenter is evidently the asker reacting to recommendations ('seem like the obvious choice ... Thanks'), should their picks be firsthand by default or none as not-yet-tried?
Is 'not the best or worst price' a neutral value verdict or lukewarm (negative) like 'fine'?
Are multi-vendor food markets such as Queens Night Market or Smorgasburg mentions, or venues like the rubric's non-places?
Is a joking gatekeeping reply ('you be quiet now', 'don't tell anyone') under a recommendation an endorsement of the recommended place?
When a place is named only to identify a person ('the Una Pizza Napoletana guy'), is it a name-in-passing mention or part of a person reference?
When a commenter's past firsthand praise is overridden by someone else's report of decline, is the current verdict firsthand or secondhand?
Should a bare list answer to a dish question ('best chicken salad sandwich?') carry that dish as a dish entry, and at what level?
Should a chain's announced-but-not-yet-open new branch set status 'opened', or stay null with a note?
Which aspect takes a complaint about format or menu structure (prix-fixe only, no a la carte): service as 'how the place is run', or overall?
Is 'terrible' / 'awful experience' very_negative or negative under the owner's extremes-only calibration?
Is enthusiasm about an untried new place ('so cool, can't wait to try') a stated positive opinion or opinion none?

Pig and Khao is closed according to a reply the model could not see; the missed object records status closed, but should a list recommendation of a since-closed place be scored as positive in the past?
When a commenter's only visit was years ago but they endorse current criticism, is the timeframe current or past?
Is a plain list of names given as examples of a trend (answering 'which places do you mean?') endorse like a list item under a recommendation request, or opinion none?
Is a suitability caveat ('not somewhere I'd take a young kid') a complaint that lowers atmosphere, or a neutral fit note?
Does a prediction that a place will get worse (e.g. after a private-equity deal) count as a current negative verdict?
Is hyperbole without a comparison ('to die for', 'unreal') positive, or very_positive like 'god tier' and 'life-changing'?
Is a sentimental-occasion anecdote ('a friend proposed there, it'll never close. Sweet.') a positive verdict on the place or opinion none?
Is 'the closest substitute, but not the same' a negative (comparison loser) verdict, or mild praise?
When the only judgment is a wait aspect ('free tables at 4', 'never had a problem walking in'), should overall follow it or stay null as a tip?
Is a restaurant group (Unapologetic Foods) a mention when criticized, or a company outside the place list?
Should a boycott over a company's politics (not food or service) lower overall at all, given rankings are about the food place?
Does trend cover a change in a single aspect such as booking difficulty, or only the overall verdict?
Is 'that sounds amazing' about an untried place secondhand (based on the parent's report) or experience none (not yet tried)?
Should a verdict from a visit years ago ('I used to work a few blocks away') be timeframe past when the comment gives no sign the place changed?
Should an unnamed place the commenter can't recall ('that place on Christopher St around the corner') be a mention when no name appears anywhere in the context?
When the only judgment is about one aspect (here the wait), should overall follow it as the strongest point or stay null? Haiku leaves it null; I followed 'strongest point'.
Is a reply that only excuses a place's flaw ('it's a small business, one person doing everything') a judgment of the place, or a fact with opinion none?
Should a closed place with no verdict at all still get timeframe past, as rule 10 says, when there are no levels for it to describe?
When a place loses a comparison about its food ('X is better'), should the loser's taste be set, or only overall?
Is 'looks amazing' about photos of a place the commenter has not tried a stated positive verdict, or opinion none?
Is 'best on the UES' (a neighborhood-limited superlative) broad enough for very_positive?
Is a mild lament like 'too bad it closed' enough for a positive verdict, or only an explicit 'I miss it'?
When the only judgment is on one aspect (value here, wait in Q0209), should overall follow it or stay null? Judges so far have done both.
Does a reply saying 'I did' file a health complaint about the post's place count as a negative verdict on it, when the commenter may not be the poster?
Whether a reply that answers the post's question about a named place only with a general rule (no name, no judgment) counts as an opinion-none mention of that place.
Whether an unnamed reply that implicitly ranks the post's place below an unnamed alternative counts as a comparison loser (negative) or as no mention.
Whether a ranked list of recommendations ('A, B, C, D in that order') makes the lower-ranked picks comparison losers (negative) or keeps them all as endorsements.
Whether music/comedy clubs that serve drinks (The Groove, Terra Blues, Comedy Cellar) are bars (mentions) or venues (not places).
Whether a bookable room or counter inside a restaurant (the Modern's Kitchen Table) is its own mention or part of the restaurant's mention.
When one location of a still-open chain closes, whether the chain mention gets status closed / timeframe past.
Whether 'do your worst' framing on an enemy-recommendation thread makes a seconded pick very_negative or only negative.
Whether food poisoning should also set taste (the food) very_negative, or only overall.
Whether Zabar's (a gourmet food store that sells bagels and has a cafe) counts as a place or as an excluded store.
Whether a booking tip like 'book at the specific time slots open' is wait negative (like 'be there by 11:30') when it answers 'easiest to get a reservation'.
Whether 'barely any seating' / 'no seating' is wait (getting a table) or atmosphere (the room).
Whether 'replace X with Y' tells others to avoid X (avoid true) or is only a comparison loss.
Whether a reaction to a post photo ('real mood') counts as a mention of the place the photo most likely shows.
Whether a comparison loser on bookability alone ('Carbone picks you') gets overall negative or only wait negative.
Whether an insincere superlative walked back in favor of an unnamed favorite makes the place a negative comparison loser or leaves overall null.
Whether 'temporarily closed' should set status closed or stay null, since status has no temporary value.
Whether a chain's visibly declining business (empty stores, closures) counts as trend declined when quality isn't mentioned.
Whether a bare 'RIP X' is a fond (positive) verdict like 'I miss it' or only a closure fact.
Does a 'go to A instead' suggestion motivated by fit (casualness for a tween) rather than quality count as a comparison that makes B negative?
When a post announces one location of a chain is closing and the comment is about another location, should status be closed?
'avoid the Times Sq location' of a chain otherwise called worth a visit: avoid stays false for the place?
'You've basically listed the standard tourist spots' knocks the post's list collectively without naming them; are those places mentions?
A remembered favorite that moved and changed its offering ('now they only sell caviar. So lame'): rule 9 current negative, or rule 10 remembered verdict with timeframe past?
Jazz clubs that serve food and drink (Birdland, Iridium) are called 'venues' in the comment; are they bars (mentions) or venues (excluded)?
Is 'one of the best meals we've had lately' a broad superlative (very_positive) or does 'lately' make it positive?
Does a bare pick answering 'where did you have the best X?' inherit the superlative (very_positive) from the question's framing, or stay an endorsement?
A list posted under 'terrible restaurants with great reviews' followed by 'I've always had great experiences here': does thread framing make the list negative, or does the explicit praise win?
Are 'terrible' and 'awful' extremes (very_negative) or strong plain knocks (negative) under the owner's calibration?
Whether enthusiasm about a dish the commenter has not yet tried ('sounds FIRE') counts as stated or endorse is not decided by the rubric.
Whether a wait complaint from someone who has not yet been, with no other verdict, should set overall negative or leave it null is not decided by the rubric.
Zabar's is a gourmet grocery store that sells bagels; the rubric excludes grocery stores, but it is discussed here as a bagel source, so whether it counts is unclear.
When one branch of a chain closes, the rubric does not say whether status should be closed on the chain mention or left null.
When the praised place is only 'this place' and the comment that named it is deleted, the rubric does not say whether to keep an unnamed mention or drop it.
Zabar's is a grocery store with an attached cafe; when the cafe is what is meant, the rubric's grocery-store exclusion is unclear.

'Great at what they do great' plus 'a ton of things that are pretty mid', applied to Chinatown spots in general, reads as hit-or-miss (neutral), but the rubric does not say whether a generalization should count against the named place.
An unnamed, unidentifiable place ('a place on rivington') with a strong complaint: the rubric does not say whether it is a mention.
Whether a pedantic category objection ('it's not a slice') counts as a complaint about the place or is opinion-free.
How to treat praise for an untried place based on a photo ('looks so good, never been'): stated with experience none, or endorse.
Whether a sexual-innuendo joke replying to a price complaint ('if I'm going to lick a chalupa I'm not paying for it') is a value judgment or opinion-free.
Whether reporting a place to the Health Department over kitchen hygiene is an extreme (very_negative) verdict without extreme words, and whether hygiene belongs under service.
Whether 'terrible' alone counts as an extreme (very_negative) or a plain negative; the calibration list does not name it.
When a commenter says they like a place very much but it is not worth the money, is not worth it a bottom line (negative) or a balanced verdict (neutral)?
Does a nostalgic joke reply under a recommendation (memories, or lack thereof) count as an endorsement or as opinion none?
When a bare recommendation names a dish as the answer (the X at Y), is the dish level positive like get the X, or null as only named?
When vendors are listed as examples of Smorgasburg alumni that Redditors can enjoy, is that an endorsement or a name in passing?
Is it not that bad used to defend a place against a knock still lukewarm and negative, or does the defensive framing make it positive?
Do gourmet food stores with deli counters, like Zabar, count as delis (mentions) or as grocery stores (not places)?
Should a general money complaint about a whole category (100 dollars for a steak is wacky) lower value for the specific places the commenter just named in that category?
When one location of a still-open chain closes, should the mention carry status closed, or only a note that a location closed?
When the comparison winner is framed as a low bar (even Chipotle is better), is the winner positive by default, neutral, or negative?
Are health-code violations and shutdowns a service complaint (how the place is run) or an overall-only complaint?
Is a chain named only as a supermarket product brand (frozen Arbys curly fries) a mention of the chain?
Is a food court or food hall (Food Gallery 32, Smorgasburg) a mention in its own right, or only its stalls?
Is a ping-pong bar like Spin a bar (mention) or a venue (not a place)?
Does a superlative about one dish (serves the best baked ziti) make the place overall very_positive?
Does clarifying another commenter complaint (they meant the partnership, here is the link) count as a secondhand negative opinion or as a fact?
Gourmet Garage, Citarella and Jefferson Market are gourmet grocers with prepared food; are they grocery stores (not places) or delis?
Is a former go-to offered as a current recommendation ('used to work here and my go tos were X') timeframe past or current?
When an agreement reply ('Get Out Of My Head!') mostly agrees with the parent's analogy rather than its restaurant verdict, does rule 8 still carry the parent's verdict on the place?
When a terse reply ('Damn if it aint delicious though') could point at the parent's place or the post's place, should the extractor prefer the post's subject?
Is 'terrible' with nothing else extreme enough for very_negative, or negative under the strict calibration?
Does hyperbole like 'should be burned to the ground' count as telling others to avoid the place?
When a comment says it would rather go to B for 'less the headache' than A, should the unspecified headache count as wait?
Is a best-time-to-go tip given in reply to 'those lines are brutal' wait negative (like 'be there by 11:30') or opinion none?
